affected_system: pedestrian right-of-way, crossings, sidewalks, and accessible routes
alternatives: rank verified high-consequence candidates for pedestrian safety and accessibility treatment portfolio
select a risk-, equity-, and lifecycle-balanced portfolio for pedestrian safety and accessibility treatment portfolio
pair exposure-, severity-, access-, and equity-weighted project optimization with an explicit stop, review, and escalation rule
assumptions: Crash, conflict, barrier, sidewalk, crossing, and demand data have explicit observation processes.
Accessibility is evaluated across route continuity, slope, surface, crossing, and obstruction dimensions.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
baseline: fund only already-committed work for pedestrian safety and accessibility treatment portfolio.

constraints.description: The pedestrian safety and universal accessibility prioritize must respect declared capital, operating, maintenance, and delivery budgets.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

decision_cadence: recompiled at each planning cycle and after material evidence change
decision_owner: vision-zero director and accessibility compliance officer
decision_question: Which crossing, signal, curb-ramp, sidewalk, lighting, and speed treatments should be funded first?

independence_key.binding_constraint: The pedestrian safety and universal accessibility prioritize must respect declared capital, operating, maintenance, and delivery budgets.
independence_key.decision_object: pedestrian safety and accessibility treatment portfolio
independence_key.evidence_gate: Evidence for pedestrian safety and accessibility treatment portfolio passes documented checks for cost, benefit, service life, dependencies, deliverability, and maintenance burden.
independence_key.intervention_mechanism: exposure-, severity-, access-, and equity-weighted project optimization
independence_key.primary_outcome: expected severe conflict and inaccessible-route burden

intended_claim: A versioned prioritize design for comparing declared alternatives affecting pedestrian safety and accessibility treatment portfolio, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: expected severe conflict and inaccessible-route burden
distributional gap in expected severe conflict and inaccessible-route burden
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not present modeled risk reduction as prevented injuries.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Evidence for pedestrian safety and accessibility treatment portfolio passes documented checks for cost, benefit, service life, dependencies, deliverability, and maintenance burden.

title: Prioritize pedestrian safety and accessibility treatments
transportability_risks: Street design, enforcement, mobility-device needs, exposure, and reporting vary by place.
Crash-only models underrepresent near misses and unreported accessibility barriers.
